A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete and readable, including their appendices, and describe the same DNL/1P-DNL research. Algorithms, experiments, and illustrations can be matched despite the changed title and substantial expansion. Internal reporting inconsistencies limit some numerical interpretations, but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-corruption experiments on ImageNet and four additional image-classification datasets, together with scoring, layer-selection, and selective-defense experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original vision experiments and reports additional language-model, text-classification, detection, segmentation, and defense results.

M1.justification: The core magnitude ranking, hybrid 1P-DNL score, and vision sign-flip procedure remain unchanged. v2 adds exponent-MSB attack variants and describes a gray-box search for opposite-sign decoded codewords when attacking DeepNcode (Section 6 and Appendix C). These are limited procedural extensions to the retained algorithms.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates image classification on ImageNet, DTD, FGVC-Aircraft, Food101, and Stanford Cars. v2 retains this coverage and adds mathematical reasoning on MATH-500, text classification on GLUE's MRPC/QNLI/SST-2, and object detection and instance segmentation on COCO 2017.

E2.justification: The existing BFA, DeepHammer, ZeBRA, and pruning-score comparators remain. BFA is newly included in the MobileNet-V2 comparison (v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 6). v2 also broadens defense comparisons to RA-BNN/binarization, with numerical results in Table 9, and reported DeepNcode and weight-scaling evaluations in Section 6.

E3.justification: New protocols include a fixed 50-question MATH-500 subset with answer verification, first-five-block versus all-layer targeting, and language-model flip budgets extending to 100. COCO evaluation uses bounding-box and mask AP/AP50 with backbone-only corruption. The new BFA defense experiment varies protection fractions and evaluates budgets of 1–10 flips, complementing the retained 100,000-random-flip stress test.

E4.justification: The original scoring, kernel, layer-selection, model-size, and random-protection analyses are retained, sometimes relocated. v2 adds sign-versus-exponent comparisons, language-model layer-scope tests, expert-routing and corrupted-generation case studies, detection failure examples, and tests of defenses against targeted attacks. These substantially expand analysis of failure mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix F newly reports 1P-DNL results over ten random seeds on five architectures, with an accuracy-reduction standard deviation of 0.02. Section 6 specifies three BFA runs per flip budget. The earlier best-of-five baseline annotation remains. These are added repeat-count and uncertainty disclosures; no increase from a previously specified run count is established.

E6.justification: New results include Qwen3-30B-A3B falling from 78% to 0% accuracy after two sign flips, COCO AP degradation, and binary ResNet-18 AR(10)=96.50%. Tables 10–11 add detailed ImageNet curves. Existing comparison entries also change: BFA/ResNet-50 reaches a reported 99.7% reduction at 11 flips in v1 Table 3 versus five in v2 Table 6. These are reported additions and revisions; inconsistent precision descriptions and summary-versus-detailed values prevent treating them as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's Taylor-inspired scoring formula, v2 introduces formal bit-string attack definitions, a quadratic-loss derivation of magnitude targeting, a claimed curvature-based lower bound, covariance-based kernel-cancellation reasoning, and a Lipschitz amplification bound. These add substantive mathematical assumptions and derivations while retaining the original AR/mAR definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly broaden the central vulnerability claim from evaluated vision classifiers to reasoning and MoE language models, detection, and segmentation. v2 adds defense evasion as a main contribution, claiming circumvention of binarization, encoding, and weight scaling. The original data-free attack and selective-protection contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the relative strength of sign and exponent attacks as domain-dependent, develops hidden-state propagation explanations for MoE failures, and distinguishes semantic errors from localization failures. It explicitly treats early-layer amplification as motivation rather than an optimality proof. New limitations address partially writable or sharded models and numerical-format dependence.

D1.justification: v2 adds exact ImageNet model-variant listings, sources for the new language and detection models, attacked MoE layer/expert/weight locations, and attribution of the binary-network reproduction to the RA-BNN recipe. These improve technical traceability, but do not provide a complete reproduction specification. Both versions retain the same promise to release code upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through encoding, weight-scaling, and binary-network defense literature, language and dense-prediction research, and additional pruning/Lipschitz references. It explicitly identifies the hybrid score as an application of existing pruning saliency under an adversarial one-pass budget. The original BFA/DeepHammer/ZeBRA comparison remains central.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around cross-domain vulnerability. The results become a domain-organized section, attack comparisons precede defenses, and appendices are reorganized. Existing kernel examples and the 1P-DNL pseudocode move from the main text into appendices.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 2–4 are merged into v2 Figure 2, while v1 Figure 6 and Table 1 become the composite Figure 4. v2 adds generation and detection examples, restructures attack-comparison tables, and introduces multiple new result tables, including complete per-model curves. Several original model-size and defense plots are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable evidence beyond v1's classification-only evaluation and random-flip defense tests, including targeted BFA testing and seed reporting. However, Section 6 claims 1% protection nullifies BFA on every model while Table 5 reports 44.30% remaining reduction for MobileNet-V2. AlexNet's 1P-DNL AR(10) is also 93.2% in Table 6 but 50.8% in Table 11 without reconciled settings. These inconsistencies affect central claims and numerical traceability, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
